summary: safeGit now returns an object with code, stdout and stderr, and no longer throws when git fails. The change also exports the new GitResult type from the core package.

findings.title: safeGit return type changed but callers still expect a string
findings.problem: safeGit now resolves to a GitResult object instead of the stdout string. currentBranch in packages/cli/src/branch.ts:7 still calls name.trim(), and changedFiles in packages/cli/src/status.ts:6 still calls out.split().
findings.consequence: In currentBranch, trim throws a TypeError, its catch swallows it, and it always returns null. The CLI in main.ts then always prints "not a git repository" and exits 1.
findings.fix: Update currentBranch and changedFiles to read result.stdout in the same change. Another option is to keep a string-returning wrapper for existing callers.

findings.title: Removed throw breaks callers that rely on git failures
findings.problem: safeGit now catches every git failure and returns a non-zero code instead of throwing. currentBranch in packages/cli/src/branch.ts:8 detects a missing repository only through that throw.
findings.consequence: If currentBranch reads stdout but not code, it returns an empty string outside a repository instead of null. main.ts then carries on, and changedFiles reports zero changes instead of an error.
findings.fix: Make currentBranch and changedFiles check result.code and handle non-zero codes. For example, currentBranch should return null when the code is not 0.

findings.title: Changed safeGit behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: This change gives safeGit a new return shape and a new error path. No test file in the repository exercises safeGit.
findings.consequence: Nothing would catch a regression in the code or stderr mapping. The broken callers also went unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for safeGit covering a successful command and a failing command. Also add tests for currentBranch outside a repository.
